                      [32m'Starting with Wasp 0.24, the Wasp DSL is now retired in favor of the Wasp Spec: a\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# 5. Querying the Database - Wasp - ContextQMD\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-14, [Read more](https://contextqmd.com/libraries/wasp/versions/0.22.0/pages/web/versioned_docs/version-0.11.8/tutorial/05-queries)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We need to add a **query** declaration to `main.wasp` so that Wasp knows it exists:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query getTasks {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Specifies where the implementation for the query function is.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Use `@server` to import files inside the `src/server` folder.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'// Tell Wasp that this query reads from the `Task` entity.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'By doing this, Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Even though you are using TypeScript and plan to implement this query in `src/server/queries.ts`, you still need to import it using a `.js` extension.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'This is only needed when importing `@server@` files.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Queries and actions are NodeJS functions that are executed on the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Therefore, we put them in the `src/server` folder.'[39m

                    text: [32m'# GitHub - wasp-lang/wasp: The batteries-included full-stack framework for the AI era.                     type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# wasp-lang/wasp v0.15.0 on GitHub\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Wasp 0.15.0 ships a preview feature that lets you define your app in\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: 2020-09-30, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/wasp-lang/wasp/issues/64)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This means following:\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Therefore you can define your database model (called Entity in Wasp) using the Prisma Schema Language (PSL) inside of Wasp.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Prisma transactions - Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-07-21, last updated: 2025-08-25, [Read more](https://www.answeroverflow.com/m/1331321118036070511)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':wave: ---------------------- To use Prisma transactions in Wasp, you can access the Prisma client directly and utilize its transaction capabilities.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Here's how you can do it: 1.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'Import the Prisma client in your server-side code:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'2. Use the\n'[39m +
                      [32m"`import prisma from '@wasp/dbClient'`\n"[39m +
                      [32m'`$transaction` method provided by Prisma to perform multiple operations within a transaction.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`const [posts, totalPosts] = await prisma.$transaction([`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'context.entities.Post.findMany({\n'[39m +

                      [32m'}),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"It's important to note that you should typically use transactions within Wasp actions or queries, where you have access to the\n"[39m +
                      [32m'`const [posts, totalPosts] = await prisma.$transaction([`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'context.entities.Post.findMany({\n'[39m +

                      [32m'}),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'context.entities.Post.count(),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'])\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`context.entities` object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you're working outside of these contexts, you can use\n"[39m +

                      [32m'`context.entities`.\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# 5. Querying the Database - Wasp - ContextQMD\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-13, [Read more](https://contextqmd.com/libraries/wasp/versions/0.22.0/pages/web/versioned_docs/version-0.17/tutorial/05-queries)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The primary way of working with Entities in Wasp is with Queries and Actions, collectively known as ***Operations* **.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Queries are used to read an entity, while Actions are used to create, modify, and delete entities.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const getTasks: GetTasks<void, Task[]> = async (args, context) => {\n'[39m +

                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<ShowForTs> Wasp automatically generates the types `GetTasks` and `Task` based on the contents of `main.wasp`: - `Task` is a type corresponding to the `Task` entity you defined in `schema.prisma`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Query function parameters:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'The arguments the caller passes to the Query.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Its type depends on the Query declaration.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Since the Query declaration in `main.wasp` says that the `getTasks` Query uses `Task` entity, Wasp injected a Prisma client for the `Task` entity as `context.entities.Task` - we used it above to fetch all the tasks from the database.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Introduction to Swarm: Building full-stack apps with Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-11-16, last updated: 2025-11-19, [Read more](https://dev.to/genyus/introduction-to-swarm-building-full-stack-apps-with-wasp-1nc5)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Prisma Schema\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The first step is to define any necessary entities in our\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schema.prisma\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'file:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'respectively.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { Task } from "wasp/entities";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { HttpError } from "wasp/server";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import type { CreateTask } from "wasp/server/operations";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const createTask: CreateTask<Pick<Task, "description" | "userId"> & Partial<Pick<Task, "isDone">>> = async (data, context) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'try {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const createdTask = await context.entities.Task.create({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'data: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...data,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return createdTask;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'} catch (error) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'console.error("Failed to create Task:", error);\n'[39m +
                      [32m"throw new HttpError(500, `Failed to create Task${error instanceof Error ? `: ${error.message}` : ''}`);\n"[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Database Migration Problem - Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-01-11, last updated: 2026-03-25, [Read more](https://www.answeroverflow.com/m/1327547697057763419)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"In development, when you make changes to your Prisma schema (like renaming a field), Wasp uses Prisma's\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'migrate dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'command, which is interactive and prompts for confirmation on potentially destructive changes.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is why you see the confirmation message in your local environment.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"However, in production, Wasp uses Prisma's\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'migrate deploy\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'command, which is designed for non-interactive environments like CI/CD pipelines.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This command only applies pending migrations and does not generate new ones or prompt for user input.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To address this problem and ensure your production database is properly migrated, you should consider the following steps:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Always create and commit migration files in your development environment before deploying to production.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Run\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp db migrate-dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'locally, which will generate the necessary migration files.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Commit these migration files to your version control system.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. Ensure your deployment process includes running migrations before starting the application.'[39m

                    text: [32m'# Queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-13, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/data-model/operations/queries)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You declare queries in the Wasp file and implement them using NodeJS.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp not only runs these queries within the server's context but also creates code that enables you to call them from any part of your codebase, whether it's on the client or server side.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create a Query, you must:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and call it directly.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The usage doesn't change depending on whether the Query is authenticated or not.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { getAllTasks, getFilteredTasks } from "wasp/client/operations"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...#### The useQuery hook​\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# React Query questions - Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-07-30, last updated: 2026-03-25, [Read more](https://www.answeroverflow.com/m/1267894500659953716)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':wave: ---------------------- In Wasp, the cache keys are handled internally and are not expected to be supplied by the user.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is done by the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'useQuery\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'hook, which is a thin wrapper around the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'hook from Wasp accepts three arguments:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m', and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'is the client-side query function generated by Wasp based on a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'object, which you can use to change the default behavior for this particular Query (**source**(https://wasp-lang.dev/docs/data-model/operations/queries#the-usequery-hook-1)).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you need to access the Query cache key, you can do so by accessing the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'queryCacheKey\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'property on any Query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Here is an example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { getTasks } from 'wasp/client/operations'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'const queryKey = getTasks.queryCacheKey\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Please note that these options are provided by React Query and not Wasp.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp uses React Query under the hood for data fetching and caching, and it provides a thin wrapper around the'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# can i implement an algorithm that fetches data on the client side\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-09-21, last updated: 2026-03-25, [Read more](https://www.answeroverflow.com/m/1286985455430008875)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':wave: ---------------------- Yes, you can implement an algorithm that fetches data on the client side using Wasp.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp provides several ways to fetch data on the client side.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Queries**: Wasp generates client-side functions that automatically take care of serialization, network calls, and cache invalidation.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You can use these functions to call server code like it's a regular function.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'Here is an example of how to use a query in a React component:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { getTasks, useQuery } from 'wasp/client/operations'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export const MainPage = () => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const { data: tasks, isLoading, error } = useQuery(getTasks)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{tasks && <TasksList tasks={tasks} />}\n'[39m +
                      [32m"{isLoading && 'Loading...'}\n"[39m +
                      [32m"{error && 'Error: ' + error}\n"[39m +
                      [32m'</div>\n'[39m +
                      [32m')\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp/client/api\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'to make API calls from your client.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can call this query on the client side like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { getTasks } from 'wasp/client/operations'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'const tasks = await getTasks()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Overriding Default Behaviour...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2025-11-23, [Read more](https://wasp-docs-on-main.pages.dev/docs/0.18.0/project/client-config)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can change the options for a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**single** Query using the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`options` object, as described here.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp's\n"[39m +
                      [32m'`useQuery` hook uses\n'[39m +
                      [32m"`react-query`'s\n"[39m +
                      [32m'`useQuery` hook under the hood.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Since\n'[39m +
                      [32m"`react-query` comes configured with aggressive but sane default options, you most likely won't have to change those defaults for all Queries.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'If you do need to change the global defaults, you can do so inside the client setup function.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp exposes a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`configureQueryClient` hook that lets you configure\n'[39m +
                      [32m"*react-query*'s\n"[39m +
                      [32m'`QueryClient` object:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"`import { configureQueryClient } from 'wasp/client/operations'`\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export default async function mySetupFunction() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"`import { configureQueryClient } from 'wasp/client/operations'`\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export default async function mySetupFunction(): Promise<void> {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'some setup\n'[39m +
                      [32m'configureQueryClient({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'defaultOptions: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'queries: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'staleTime: Infinity,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Make sure to pass in an object expected by the\n'[39m +
                      [32m"`QueryClient`'s constructor, as\n"[39m +
                      [32m'explained in\n'[39m +
                      [32m"react-query's docs."[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# 5. Querying the Database\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-01, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/tutorial/queries)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To list the tasks, you must:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Create a Query that fetches the tasks from the database.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Update the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'to use that Query and display the results.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import type { GetTasks } from "wasp/server/operations";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"While we implement Queries on the server, Wasp generates client-side functions that automatically take care of serialization, network calls, and cache invalidation, allowing you to call the server code like it's a regular function.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'useQuery\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- Wasp's useQuery React hook, which is based on react-query's hook with the same name.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Notice how you don't need to annotate the type of the Query's return value: Wasp uses the types you defined while implementing the Query for the generated client-side function.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'This is **full-stack type safety**: the types on the client always match the types on the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We could have called the Query directly using\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m', but the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'hook makes it reactive: React will re-render the component every time the Query changes.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Remember that Wasp automatically refreshes Queries whenever the data is modified.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-10, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1import { app, page, query, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec";\n'[39m +

                      [32m'1import { getTasks, useQuery } from "wasp/client/operations";\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Wasp × AI駆動開発で爆速フルスタック開発を体験した話\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-03-03, last updated: 2026-08-13, [Read more](https://zenn.dev/branch/articles/004ab27dcba328)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Waspは**Queries**（データ取得）と**Actions**（データ更新）という2種類のサーバー関数を持ちます。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// src/boards/queries.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { type GetBoard } from "wasp/server/operations";\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### クライアントからの呼び出し\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// src/boards/BoardPage.tsx\n'[39m +

Wasp compiles a declarative `main.wasp` file together with your React/Node code into a full-stack app, using Prisma for the database and React Query for client-side data fetching. Wasp automatically invalidates a Query\'s cache whenever an Action that declares the *same* Entity runs. This automatic, entity-based invalidation is convenient but coarse: it does not understand *derived* or *relational* data, so a computed Query that depends on another entity only through a relation will NOT be refreshed automatically. Your job is to build a small task board that relies on automatic invalidation where it works and falls back to explicit React Query cache management where it does not.  A Wasp project skeleton already exists at the project path. You must implement the data model, the Operations, the database seed, and the page.  ## Requirements - Model two entities in the Prisma schema: a **Project** (has a name and many tasks) and a **Task** (has a title, a done flag, and belongs to a Project). - Implement a Query `getTasks` that returns every task (with its id, title, done state and project id). - Implement a computed/derived Query `getProjectStats` that returns, for every project, an object with the project\'s id, its name, the total number of tasks in that project, and the number of done tasks in that project. - Implement an Action `addTask` that creates a new task in a given project, and an Action `toggleTask` that flips a task\'s done state. - Build a single page (mounted at `/`) that lists every project together with its live statistics, lists all tasks, lets the user add a task to a project, and lets the user toggle a task\'s done state. Every displayed value must update reactively after an Action, WITHOUT a full page reload. - Provide a database seed that populates the initial board (see the hint below for the exact required data).  ## Implementation Hints - Wasp automatically invalidates a Query whenever an Action that shares one of its declared entities runs. Use this for the plain task list, but remember it only fires on exact entity overlap: declare the entity `getTasks` reads so Wasp keeps it fresh automatically. - `getProjectStats` is an intentionally decoupled aggregate: it MUST be declared so that it depends only on the `Project` entity (do NOT add `Task` to its entity list). Because of that, adding or toggling a task will NOT automatically refresh it. You must keep it up to date on the client yourself using React Query\'s cache mechanisms: obtain the `QueryClient` (react-query is bundled with Wasp and importable from `@tanstack/react-query`) and invalidate/refetch the stats Query after the relevant Actions. A Wasp client Query object exposes its cache key via its `queryCacheKey` property, which you can use as the react-query query key. - Compute the derived statistics from the database (e.g. via the Project entity\'s Prisma relation / relation counts); do not maintain a separate hand-rolled counter table. - Use a local SQLite database (the default dev database). Run `wasp db migrate-dev` after changing the schema so it is applied, and commit the generated migration. - Add exactly one Wasp database seed named `devSeed` (declared under the app\'s `db.seeds`). It must be safe to run repeatedly and must always leave the database in exactly this state: a project named `Work` containing two tasks titled `Ship release` (done) and `Write docs` (not done); and a project named `Home` containing one task titled `Buy groceries` (not done). Running it should clear any prior projects/tasks first so the result is deterministic. The seed is run with `wasp db seed devSeed`. - Project path: /home/user/taskboard - Start command (run from the project path): `wasp start`. This serves the web client at http://localhost:3000 (the API server runs on port 3001). The first build can take a while before the page becomes available. - The page must render the following stable, machine-checkable markers so the UI can be inspected reliably (attributes are on the element whose text is read):   - For each project, show its name, and an element with attribute `data-testid="stat-total-<projectId>"` whose text content is exactly the project\'s total task count as a number, and an element with attribute `data-testid="stat-done-<projectId>"` whose text content is exactly the project\'s done-task count as a number.   - For each task, an element with attribute `data-testid="task-<taskId>"`, and a clickable button with attribute `data-testid="toggle-<taskId>"` that toggles that task\'s done state.   - For each project, a clickable button with attribute `data-testid="add-task-<projectId>"` that adds a new task to that project (the new task\'s title may be any non-empty string).   - `<projectId>` and `<taskId>` are the numeric database ids of the project and task.             [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Before executing the command, please follow these steps:\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`). For instance, if one operation must complete before another starts (like mkdir before cp, Write before executeCommand for git operations, or git add before git commit), run these operations sequentially instead.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +

Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes. If the commit succeeds but you notice that files were modified by the pre-commit hook, you MUST amend your commit to include them.\n'[39m +

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how should we refactor the database schema"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to perform code reviews and leave inline comments.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent can analyze code and create review comments on specific lines.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "review the code in src/auth"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "add review comments to this file"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you want to read a specific file path, use the readFile or globFiles tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the globFiles tool instead, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Launch multiple agents tools concurrently whenever possible to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.
